title: eludite.debug.trace output
description: The lines the tracepoints printed, in order, and why collecting ended.

seq.description: The line's position in this answer, from 0.

hit.description: The point's hit count at this line (1 for its first hit).

text.description: The message as printed (cut at 1000 characters with `… (N chars)`).

truncated.description: `max_hits` was reached: the points were disabled and the debuggee keeps running.

stopped_by.description: `terminated`: the session ended (see `exit_code`). `stopped`: a visible stop (see `summary`). `hits`: `count` or `max_hits` hits. `timeout`: `wait_ms` ran out (the debuggee goes on running). `interrupted`: the person resumed, paused, stopped or restarted the debuggee while the trace collected (proposal 0001 rule 5); the lines collected so far are answered.

summary.description: With `stopped_by: stopped`: the stop summary (debug-stop-summary.output.json) within the budget parameters.

exit_code.description: With `stopped_by: terminated`: the program's exit code, when the adapter reported it.

points.description: The points, in the order given.

verified.description: The debug adapter bound it to code (false: it never printed and `message` may say why).

message.description: Why the adapter did not bind it.

overhead_ms_per_hit.description: When the debugger emulated the tracepoints (the adapter has no log points): the mean time from a hit's stop to its resume, in milliseconds. Absent when the adapter printed the lines.

emulated.description: The debugger emulated the tracepoints (a stop and a resume per hit).

generation.description: The session generation the trace ran in.
